DI BAGONG PILJP'NAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City ph s. 2021 OILG OPINION NO. og JAN 11 MR. ELISEO JOSELITO MONROY II eliseomonroysintl@qmail.com Dear Mr. Monroy II: This pertains to your earlier email conceming the propriety of the move to privatize Tanjay Water District (TWD) of Tanjay, Negros Oriental. In the strictest sense of identity and existence, water districts are primarily established as govemment-owned and controlled corporations (GOCCs). It is formed following the requirements under Section 6 of Presidential Decree 198, viz: Section 6. Formation of District. - This Act is the source of authorization and power to form and maintain a district. Once formed, a district is subject to the provisions of this Act and not under the jurisdiction of any political subdivision. To form a district, the legislative body of any city, municipality or province shall enact a resolution containing the following: (a) The name of the local water district, which shall include the name of the city, municipality, or province, or region thereof, served by said system, followed by the words "Water District". (b) A description of the boundary of the district. In the case of a city or municipality, such boundary may include all lands within the city or municipality. A district may include one or more municipalities, cities or provinces, or portions thereof. (c) A statement of intent to transfer any and all waterworks and/or sewerage facilities owned by such city, municipality or province to such district pursuant to a contract authorized by Section 31 (b) of this Title. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54



(d) A statement identifying the purpose for which the district is formed, which shall include those purposes outlined in Section 5 above. (e) The names of the initial directors of the district with the date of expiration of term of office for each. (f) A statement that the district may only be dissolved on the grounds and under the conditions set forth in Section 44 of this Title. (g) A statement acknowledging the powers, rights and obligations as set forth in Section 36 of this Title. Nothing in the resolution of formation shall state or infer that the local legislative body has the power to dissolve, alter or affect the district beyond that specifically provided for in this Act. If two or more cities, municipalities or provinces, or any combination thereof, desire to form a single district, a similar resolution shall be adopted in each city, municipality and province. The number and qualifications of the Board of Directors of a local water district is likewise provided under Section 8, Chapter Ill, of PD 198. Per the Local Water Utilities Administration (LWUA), a duly organized water district is formed through the following processi: One: LWUA conducts preliminary talks and consultations with interested local govemment entities. Two: The local govemment conducts public hearings to arrive at a consensus on whether to form a water district or not. (LWUA Board Resolution No. 147, Series of 2009, amended the Guidelines for the Formation of Water Districts in Communities Without Existing Water System, and states that "LWUA shall no longer require a public hearing on water district formation as a requisite for the filing of the same.") Three: The local legislative body (the Sangguniang Bayan/Lungsod or Sangguniang Panlalawigan, as the case may be) secures nominations for candidates for the water district board of directors from business, civic, professional, education and women sectors of the community concemed. Four: The Sanggunian secretary collates all nominations and forwards the same to the appointing authority. 1 https://lwua.gov.ph/water-districts/what-is-a-water-district/

Five: The Mayor or Govemor appoints the directors. Six: The local legislative body deliberates and enacts a resolution to form a water district stating therein the name and terms of office of the duly appointed board of directors. Seven: The Mayor or Govemor approves resolution, submits the same to LWUA. Eight: LWUA reviews the resolution to determine compliance with Presidential Decree No. 198 (Provincial Water Utilities Act of 1973) and LWUA requirements. Nine: If the resolution complies with requirements, LWUA issues a Conditional Certificate of Conformance (CCC), a water district is bom and becomes eligible to avail of LWUA's comprehensive assistance program. The local water districts existence as a govemment owned and controlled corporation founded on the foregoing legal bases confirm the jurisdiction of the Commission on Audit (COA) over its operations. This fact coupled with the prescription of qualifications of the Board of Directors thereof are the govemment's way of protecting the rights and interest of its citizens over matters pertaining to water utility and resources. In that regard, privatization of local water districts is not only a blatant circumvention of the rule of law but also a means of channeling against protection of the rights of the citizenry. This position prevails in the absence of a new law allowing said privatization. As to the issue on operational autonomy of water districts, we affirm that said operation should be free from any influence of local officials pursuant to DILG Memorandum Circular 2019-032 reiterating DILG M No. 2016-1463. Incidentally, this issue of the so-called "privatization" along with joint venture agreements is timely worth discussing. The enactment of Republic Act No. 7718 in 1994, amending Republic Act No. 6957, otherwise known as the "Build Operate transfer LaW' (BOT Law), is not to be construed as the legislature's authority for the privatization of local water districts. What was authorized is simply the LGUs' entering into contracts with private entities for the financing, construction, operation, and maintenance of infrastructure projects. Although apparently, the operation of local water districts may be deemed to fall within the contemplation of "operation of infrastructure projects", the same is still not subject of PPP or JVAs by virtue of operational autonomy mandated under Paragraph 3, Section 6 of P.D. 198, to wit: Nothing in the resolution of formation shall state or infer that the local legislative body has the power to dissolve, alter or affect the district beyond that specifically provided for in this Act. 2 REITERATING DILG MC NO. 2016-146 ON THE OPERATIONAL AUTONOMY OF THE LOCAL WATER DISTRICTS 3 OPERATIONAL AUTONOMY OF THE LOCAL WATER DISTRICTS

Notwithstanding the foregoing opinion, the Department defers to any opinion that the Local Water District Administration (LWUA) may have, or any contrary ruling of the proper court, on the matter. We hope to have addressed your concem. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: . ROMEO P.
